slides.headline: A 12-year-old inherited a small chiefdom. By the time he was done, he ruled an empire that stretched from Kabul to Tibet.
Maharaja Ranjit Singh was born on November 13, 1780.
slides.body: He became the leader of a small Sikh chiefdom in Punjab at age 12, after his father's death - and over the following decades, united rival Sikh factions and built the Sikh Empire, one of the last major powers to resist British expansion in the subcontinent.

slides.headline: At its height, his empire stretched from Khyber Pass to Tibet.
slides.body: Ranjit Singh built a modernized, disciplined army trained partly by European officers, ran a famously tolerant administration that included Hindu, Muslim, and Sikh officials alike, and held off colonial encroachment for his entire 40-year reign.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is still shaped by rulers who proved a diverse, disciplined state could hold its ground.
slides.body: Ranjit Singh didn't inherit an empire - he built one from a fractured region, and ran it as one of the most stable, pluralistic powers of its era.

sources.text: Sikh Museum UK - Maharaja Ranjit Singh's 235th Birth Anniversary
